title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 172 (Pledge, pawnor and pawnee defined)

content.overview: Section 172 provides that the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called ‘pledge’. The bailor is in this case called the ‘pawnor’. The bailee is called ‘pawnee’.
content.glance: Pledge is the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise. The bailor is the pawnor; the bailee is the pawnee.
content.study: The bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called ‘pledge’. The bailor is in this case called the ‘pawnor’. The bailee is called ‘pawnee’. Current-law framing: pledge is a special form of bailment whose purpose is security.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: The bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise is called ‘pledge’. The bailor is in this case called the ‘pawnor’. The bailee is called ‘pawnee’.

examples.title: Goods as security
examples.body: A delivers goods to B as security for a debt. This is a pledge: A is pawnor, B is pawnee.

hypotheticals.question: Goods are delivered as security for repayment of a loan. Is this a pledge?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 172 defines pledge as the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise.

examples: Delivery of jewellery as security for a loan is a pledge.
distinctions: Pledge is a special bailment for security; ordinary bailment may be for other purposes.
